criteria.criterion: `make amend-msg FILE=<path>` amends HEAD with FILE's contents and the resulting commit carries the SAME `Change-Id` as before the amend — proven by a test that captures the Change-Id before and after and asserts equality.
The same test proves the naive form still loses it: `git commit --amend -F <file>` on the same fixture yields a DIFFERENT (or absent) Change-Id.
`make amend-msg` fails loudly and non-zero when HEAD carries no `Change-Id`, rather than producing a commit that will be stamped with a fresh one.
`AGENTS.md` names `make amend-msg` as the path for a rewritten commit message and states that `--amend -m` / `--amend -F` drop the Change-Id and create a duplicate Gerrit change.
